Paper: Atta et al. (2023)
Critical caveat for synthesis: Raw rice husk; no real-water, regeneration or column study. qmax = 2.47 mg/g. Isotherm dose about 90 g/L, which affects practical comparability.
Action required: Check values against full text; preserve high-dose limitation in synthesis.

Paper: Alidadi et al. (2018)
Critical caveat for synthesis: Hospital-sample tetracycline decreased from 0.25 mg/L to below HPLC detection. Single-stage desorption/regeneration only; reuse cycles not established.
Action required: Verify exact methods and whether the hospital-sample result is described accurately.

Paper: Delmond et al. (2023)
Critical caveat for synthesis: Table 3 prints modified-ash Langmuir qmax = 12,179.5 mg/g, inconsistent with measured capacities around 2.79–4 mg/g.
Action required: Do not cite the fitted qmax as reliable unless resolved against the original paper or a correction.

Paper: Conde-Cid et al. (2021)
Critical caveat for synthesis: No reliable Langmuir qmax; linear and Freundlich models were used. Solution pH was not adjusted/buffered. Pine bark, oak ash and mussel shell are different material classes.
Action required: Keep model fit and uptake distinct; record material-specific doses and uncontrolled pH.

Paper: Míguez-González et al. (2023)
Critical caveat for synthesis: Fitted qmax values are sparse or unstable for some material–antibiotic pairs. Abstract uptake around 12,000 µmol/kg must not be equated with fitted qmax.
Action required: Check model tables and units in the original PDF before using qmax.

Paper: Li et al. (2019)
Critical caveat for synthesis: The paper studies trimethoprim and diclofenac; diclofenac is an NSAID, not an antibiotic. Isotherm concentrations differ substantially from low-concentration kinetic tests.
Action required: Only include trimethoprim in antibiotic-specific synthesis; record unit conversions from µg/g to mg/g.

Paper: Mohammed-Ridha & Abdul-Ahad (2014)
DOI / source URL: No DOI confirmed from current record
Critical caveat for synthesis: The actual publication year appears to be 2014 despite a misleading filename. Table qmax values conflict with the narrative material ranking.
Action required: Verify bibliographic metadata and original data; avoid relying on the inconsistent fitted capacities until resolved.

Paper: Yao et al. (2023) — Fe/N co-doped rape-straw biochar
Critical caveat for synthesis: Langmuir qmax values are model-derived at 298–318 K (CIP 25.36–46.45 mg/g; Cu2+ 27.92–30.77 mg/g); binary qmax lower (CIP 18.84, Cu2+ 17.23 mg/g at 318 K). Matrix test is spiked tap water/groundwater at 50 mg/L each, not wastewater. Authors describe NaCl impact on CIP as negligible, although reported uptake falls 17.30 to 11.33 mg/g. Cu reduction as a proposed mechanism needs oxidation-state verification.
Action required: Keep single and binary values separate; label qmax as fitted; do not call the tests real wastewater. Recheck Supplementary Tables S1–S3, cycle-by-cycle reuse and XPS chemical-state assignment before final synthesis.

Paper: Jaria et al. (2019) — waste-derived GAC fixed bed
Critical caveat for synthesis: Only sulfamethoxazole (SMX) is an antibiotic target; carbamazepine and paroxetine are non-antibiotic comparators. Experimental curve-integrated qtotal can differ sharply from fitted Thomas/Yan q values; authors note several fitted capacities overestimate measured capacities, and curves did not reach C/C0=1 within test window.
Action required: Use SMX only in antibiotic-specific comparisons. Keep observed integrated qtotal distinct from qTH/qY and from a true saturation capacity. Record real WWTP-effluent feed as filtered and spiked, with target background below detection.

Paper: Gao et al. (2024) — KOH-activated dyeing-sludge biochar
Critical caveat for synthesis: Main text inconsistencies: SBET is 1178.4 m2/g in abstract/characterization/Table 2 but 1078.4 in one discussion sentence; Eq. (2) writes R%=(C0−Ct)/Ct×100, unlike the conventional denominator C0; isotherm method says 298 K but conclusion states qmax at 278 K; fixed-bed max 1124.2 mg/g exceeds batch Langmuir qmax 1081.3 mg/g; abstract/body label cycle-5 metrics differently (86.35% removal vs 86.88% regeneration efficiency and 86.35% retained capacity). Batch dose and real tailwater details are incomplete in the supplied main PDF.
Action required: Do not silently reconcile. Use 1178.4 m2/g only with a note that one in-text sentence prints 1078.4; flag the formula and capacity/temperature/regeneration discrepancies for SI/author verification. Treat ~$9/kg as an author-reported preliminary preparation estimate, not complete TEA/LCA; include Fenton chemical demand and spent-liquid considerations.

Paper: Jiao et al. (2024) — OTC molecularly imprinted magnetic biochar
Critical caveat for synthesis: Abstract/narrative report MBC qmax 38.84 mg/g but Table 2 gives 38.34 mg/g. Abstract gives 299 K while most methods say 25 °C. Main PDF specifies an iron-leaching test but supplies no numeric result in the accessible body. PSO fit is described as chemisorption, which is not proved by fit alone. Fig. 4a also reports OTC uptake 11.97 mg/g while its caption states 4 mg/L feed and 0.5 g/L adsorbent, implying a mass-balance ceiling of 8 mg/g even at complete removal; this value exceeds the stated ceiling.
Action required: Keep 38.34 vs 38.84 mg/g flagged; label 67.89 mg/g as fitted MBC@MIPs qmax; do not claim real wastewater/low leaching/cost feasibility. Search SI independently; user is not expected to provide SI. Resolve the Fig. 4a capacity/condition mismatch before using 11.97 mg/g; retain selectivity-factor evidence separately from this suspect uptake value.

Paper: Mosaffa et al. (2024) — bacterial-cellulose-char / CS-PEI beads
Critical caveat for synthesis: The article reports empirical q values 960.778 mg/g TET and 691.325 mg/g MET at 400 mg/L initial concentration (~0.267 g/L dose). Abstract TET removal is 99.13%, whereas body gives 99.52%. Regeneration section refers to 11 cycles but reports 96.7→89.81% “over two cycles” and 92.86% effectiveness; elsewhere it reports 63.22% after eleven cycles.
Action required: Always display 400 mg/L initial concentration and batch conditions with q values. Do not choose one regeneration figure without resolving the paper's inconsistency. No real-water test or full cost analysis in main PDF.

Paper: Masrura et al. (2024) — solvent-modified sludge biochar for human urine
Critical caveat for synthesis: Matrix was fresh human urine diluted 1:1 with DI water and spiked with antibiotics, not municipal wastewater. Capacities are µg/g at feeds of 100–1000 µg/L. Table 1 contains negative Langmuir Qm for TC on SS700 CAS and all five antibiotics on pristine SS700; these are unusable fits. Abstract says <30% removal capacity after three cycles while body gives cycle-five antibiotic-specific regeneration figures.
Action required: Use µg/g units and matrix/starting concentration explicitly; do not compare directly with mg/L-scale isotherms. Flag negative fit parameters rather than reporting them as capacities; record regeneration discrepancy; no TEA/LCA.

Paper: Hacıosmanoğlu et al. (2022) — review of natural/modified clay minerals
Critical caveat for synthesis: Review has 82 selected articles and summarizes many capacities, but key tables are in referenced supplementary Tables S1–S6 not included in uploaded main PDF. Reported review-method counts (15 real-wastewater studies, 7 continuous-flow, 0 pilot-scale) cover the review’s literature window through 2021. Historical raw-clay/GAC/CNT prices are not current market quotes, and year/grade/region basis is unclear.
Action required: Use as secondary taxonomy and citation-discovery source; verify each capacity against its primary paper before quantitative synthesis. Do not present its study counts as the 2026 state of the field or its old prices as current costs. Assistant-side SI retrieval remains a follow-up.

Paper: Wang et al. (2010) — ciprofloxacin on Ca-montmorillonite SAz-1
Critical caveat for synthesis: Reported 330 mg/g maximum capacity and ~292 mg/g observed loading use very high initial CIP concentrations (500–4,000 mg/L). Study is batch-only with duplicate tests; it does not test real wastewater, regeneration, continuous flow or cost. The direct mechanism evidence is strong: cation release vs CIP uptake slope ~0.99 (R² 0.9935), Ca2+ is the main released ion, and XRD/FTIR changes support interlayer exchange.
Action required: Use for the mechanism section, clearly label high-concentration conditions and separate fitted/reported maximum capacity from observed uptake. Do not treat this alone as evidence of trace-level wastewater performance.

Paper: Du et al. (2025) — phosphoric-acid cotton-husk biochar
Critical caveat for synthesis: The abstract labels 572.8 mg/g as maximum capacity at 25 °C; Table 3 lists experimental Qe=572.8 mg/g at 298 K, but Langmuir fitted Qm=523.0 mg/g at 298 K and 572.8 mg/g at 308 K. Real secondary pharmaceutical wastewater experiment reports EEM/COD/TOC/color changes without target-specific CIP quantification. Three-cycle capacities are given for EtOH/2 M HCl/2 M NaOH but prose-to-route order is ambiguous. Cost estimates refer to SI Table S4 and lack a transparent, harmonized cost boundary in main text.
Action required: Retain measured Qe and fitted qmax separately; do not claim target-specific CIP removal in actual effluent without analytical CIP data. Flag regeneration mapping and cost boundary. SI is an assistant-side lookup, not a user dependency.

Paper: Na et al. (2024) — pristine macadamia-nutshell biochar
Critical caveat for synthesis: The paper uses MBC to mean macadamia biochar (not magnetic biochar). Kinetic qe and Langmuir Qmax are in mmol/kg, not mg/g. Test dose is high (8 g/L), kinetics use 4 mg/L feed, isotherms 4–60 mg/L; no real wastewater, regeneration, cost, leaching or LCA. Supplementary Table S1/Fig. S1 are referenced but not in the uploaded main PDF.
Action required: Preserve native units and posterior uncertainty; keep kinetic qe distinct from fitted Qmax and identify concentration/dose with every comparison. Do not describe the material as validated in actual wastewater or as economically proven.

Paper: Zhou et al. (2024) — microwave regeneration of natural Sep/Mt
Critical caveat for synthesis: At 25 mg/L TC, observed kinetic uptake is 11.252 mg/g Sep and 20.736 mg/g Mt, while fitted Langmuir Qmax values are much higher and arise from separate 10–120 mg/L isotherms. Regeneration ratio uses Qi/Q0×100 and may exceed 100%; Fig. 15 time-optimum ratios, Fig. 16 dosage tests and Fig. 17 cycle data are different contexts. Nominal 750 W×20/25 min is not measured energy consumption. The Table 5 entropy unit/value magnitude also merits verification.
Action required: Keep observed uptake, fitted Qmax and each regeneration test context separate. Label nominal kWh as calculation from rated power/time, not measured energy intensity. Do not claim full-scale low-energy economics or pollutant mineralization; SI not supplied/retrieved.

Paper: Usama et al. (2025) — PET-derived KOH activated carbon kC1170
Critical caveat for synthesis: Fig. 3d states 120 mg/L of each target, 1 g/L adsorbent, pH 4 and 100 mL, but plotted q markers appear around 170 mg/g per target, exceeding the 120 mg/g single-target mass-balance ceiling under those conditions. Fig. 4 dose-screen q values and removal percentages also do not cleanly reconcile with C0/dose. Abstract includes a capacity q unit as mg/L although q is elsewhere mg/g. The reported LCA excludes use, disposal of spent media and desorbed antibiotics.
Action required: Do not use questionable q values in quantitative rankings without SI/author clarification; state the inconsistency. Distinguish author-reported LCA/cost from whole-life estimates; reported 5.92 kg CO2-eq/kg and US$13.75/kg are boundary- and location-dependent.

Paper: Fraiha et al. (2024) — clay/pharmaceutical adsorption review
Critical caveat for synthesis: Review Table 2 compiles mixed pharmaceutical targets and different test conditions, often with missing fields; the review concerns pharmaceuticals generally, not antibiotics only. The main PDF does not provide a reproducible systematic-search strategy/flow.
Action required: Use as narrative secondary source and citation-discovery only. Check original studies before entering capacities/removal percentages into quantitative synthesis. Do not claim the review is systematic or use its summary table as a homogeneous material ranking.

Paper: Yaqubi et al. (2021) — leached carbon-black waste and chitosan beads
Critical caveat for synthesis: Results text reports LCBW BET ~375 m²/g while conclusion reports ~275 m²/g. The powdered-TC method starts with 0.2 g in 500 mL before adding an equal volume of 50 mg/L TC solution, giving a final nominal dose of 0.2 g/L, but text states 0.4 g/L. Table 6 capacities and removal data align better with the lower final dose; fixed-bed models are described as poorly fitting. Residual V/Ni/Fe remain after leaching.
Action required: Keep both BET values and the dosage ambiguity visible. Do not promote fitted fixed-bed q to a validated dynamic capacity. No unit cost, within-study regeneration study, or full LCA; residual metal fate needs cautious discussion.

Paper: Zhu et al. (2024) — in-situ N-doped biochar from oxytetracycline fermentation residue
Critical caveat for synthesis: Printed methods equations use (Ce−C0) in qe and removal formulas, appearing to reverse signs for adsorption when Ce<C0. Main text reports 4% decline after five reuse cycles but Table 1 gives target-specific reusability percentages 96.90, 89.23, 95.08 and 95.44 without fully clear cycle mapping. SI Tables S1–S7/Figs. S1–S4 are unavailable in the uploaded PDF; no full cost/yield/energy or real wastewater data.
Action required: Flag the equation as a likely printed sign error; do not reproduce incorrectly. Keep capacity values as abstract/conclusion-reported Langmuir Qmax pending SI parameters. Report no leaching/four-gene signal only under the described assays; do not generalize to all genes/matrices or claim universal safety.

Paper: Yan et al. (2024) — review of tetracycline adsorption by biochar
Critical caveat for synthesis: Review Table 1 and real-water/regeneration sections compile primary papers with different feedstocks, concentration, pH, dose, models and matrices. Values in the review are secondary and may mix reported maxima/observed results; TOC reduction examples are not target-specific tetracycline removal.
Action required: Use for taxonomy, gaps and citation mining. Trace any quantitative claim to original paper and preserve its exact test conditions and metric; never count a review-table value as an independent experimental result.

Paper: Zango et al. (2024) — systematic review of biomass biochar/AC for antibiotic wastewater
Critical caveat for synthesis: Search ended 2024-04-30. Fig. 1 reports 305 full texts included in qualitative assessment and 162 studies included in SLR, while full-text exclusions are 54 and narrative later refers to 301 papers considered. The displayed Scopus/WoS Boolean search string lacks explicit parentheses around OR. Table 4 contains price estimates from different years and locations.
Action required: Keep search counts as author-reported with an internal discrepancy flag until clarified. Do not describe it as current 2026 evidence or use the cost table as a current comparable price list. Use citations to prioritize primary-paper screening.
